# Krate

> Krate is an open-source app runtime and AI app maker, built in Rust on Wasmtime. One small .krate file is the whole app: it runs natively on macOS, Windows and Linux with no browser or WebView inside, and the same file opens from a link in any modern browser, phones included, with nothing to install and no account. There is no separate build, package or signature for each operating system. Describe an app and Krate Studio, or Claude through the Krate connector, makes it; send it as one file or one link, the way you send a picture, and publish an update to change what the link people already have opens. In the browser it can use its own database, files the person opens or drops in, live connections, sound, and the camera, microphone and location once the person allows them. Every app starts with no access to files or the network and asks before it touches anything. Measured against an Electron app doing the same work on the same Mac, a Krate app opened a 50,000-line document in 237.1 ms instead of 611.5 ms and held it in 178.5 MiB instead of 2,299.4 MiB. Not to be confused with Rust crates (crates.io), krate.com or KrateSoft.

Krate makes apps you send like pictures: one small .krate file that opens from a link in any browser, phones included, with nothing to install, and runs natively on macOS, Windows and Linux.

## Facts

- Current release: Krate 0.6.0 (2026-11-22).
- Runtimes: macOS (Apple silicon, Intel), Windows (x64, ARM64), Linux (x86_64, arm64).
- What the recipient installs: Nothing, to open a link: the app runs in any modern browser, phones included, with no account. To run apps natively, the recipient installs the Krate runtime once for macOS, Windows or Linux, and every .krate opens from its file after that.
- Sandbox: Every app starts with no access to files or the network. Before it opens, the person sees exactly what it asks for and decides; hosts it did not declare stay unreachable, and each app keeps its own storage. Grant only what the task needs.
- Licences: the Krate runtime, format and CLI are free and open source (MIT OR Apache-2.0). Studio has separate licensing (Business Source License 1.1); see the repository license details.
- Studio: Krate Studio makes and changes apps with AI: describe the app in plain words and it writes, checks and packs it, then keep changing it by asking. Studio runs on macOS, Windows and Linux and in the browser at krate.tech/app/, and works with Claude, Codex, Grok or Gemini. Developers can also build with the krate command line and the Rust SDK.
- Make an app in Claude: Krate is a connector for Claude: add https://hub.krate.tech/mcp as a custom connector (on claude.ai, Customize > Connectors) and ask for an app in plain words. Claude writes the app; Krate compiles it, checks it and publishes it, unlisted, to the person's Krate account, and Claude answers with a link that opens it in any modern browser, phones included, with nothing to install. Krate runs no AI of its own there and never sees the conversation, only the app files Claude sends. Building needs a Krate sign-in (GitHub, Google or email). Claude Code users can install the Krate plugin: github.com/incyashraj/krate-claude-plugin.
- When to choose Krate: Choose Krate when one app has to run on Windows, macOS, Linux and in the browser without a separate build, installer and signature for each; when an Electron or Tauri app is too heavy; for a team's internal tools; when the app must work offline and keep its data on the device, print to a printer the person picks with no print dialog (PDF, PNG, or ZPL, EPL and ESC/POS for label and receipt printers), talk to serial or USB devices, read and write Excel files, or serve other devices on the local network; when an AI made the app and the people running it should decide what it may touch; and when the app should travel as one file or one link. Printing, serial, USB and serving the network run natively on macOS, Windows and Linux. Why Krate: https://krate.tech/why-krate.html
- Bundles: A .krate bundle contains a WebAssembly component and manifest, and can also carry source, SDK interfaces and assets. Full bundle bytes, uncompressed code payload, runtime download and installed runtime size are different measurements.
- Facts page: https://krate.tech/facts/

## How Krate compares

- Electron: every Electron app carries its own copy of Chromium and Node.js. A Krate app is a small WebAssembly file, and every Krate app on a computer shares one runtime installed once. In a recorded comparison on the same Mac, a Krate notes app opened a 50,000-line document in 237.1 ms (median of ten warm runs) against 611.5 ms for the Electron app MarkText, and held it in 178.5 MiB in one process against 2,299.4 MiB across four processes; with a 5,000-line document, 62.0 MiB against 366.5 MiB.
- Disk: that Krate app was 36.6 KiB against MarkText's 284.6 MiB installed. Counting the Krate runtime, installed once at 88.6 MiB and shared by every Krate app, the first app still took about a third of the disk, and each further app adds only its own file.
- Tauri: a Tauri app draws through the operating system's WebView and is built, packaged and signed separately for each operating system. A .krate file is one artifact for every operating system, draws natively with no WebView, and the same file also opens in a browser.
- A web app: a .krate opens from a link like a web page, and when it runs natively it also works offline, keeps its data on the device, prints to a chosen printer with no dialog, talks to serial and USB devices and serves other devices on the local network.
- Security: a Krate app starts with no access to files, the network or devices. It declares what it needs in its manifest, the person sees that list in plain words before it runs and decides, hosts it did not declare stay unreachable, and each app keeps its own storage. A signed app carries its publisher's Ed25519 signature, checked when it opens. A typical Electron or native desktop app runs with all of the user's permissions.
- Shipping: one file for macOS, Windows, Linux and the browser means one build, one package and one signature instead of one per operating system. Publishing gives a link, and publishing an update changes what that same link opens. Organisations can send private apps to their team, each release going out only after a second person approves it.

## Not to be confused with

Krate (krate.tech) is the Krate app runtime. It is not a Rust crate or crates.io package, and it is not related to krate.com, KrateSoft or the JavaScript project of the same name.

## Scoped benchmark

The recorded 2026-08-25 notes comparison.
MarkText 0.17.1 ARM64 vs the Krate notes replica, Apple M4, macOS 27 (build 26A5388g), on AC power; equivalent-workload comparison, not feature parity.

- Historical app bundle versus installed application: Krate 36.6 KiB; MarkText 284.6 MiB installed.
- memory, 50,000-line document: Krate 178.5 MiB, one process; MarkText 2,299.4 MiB across four processes.
- warm start to a visible window, 50,000-line document: Krate 237.1 ms median; MarkText 611.5 ms median.
- memory, 5,000-line document: Krate 62.0 MiB, one process; MarkText 366.5 MiB across four processes.

The historical Krate runtime was installed separately at 88.6 MiB. The 36.6 KiB app bundle is not the total first-install cost. Warm open is the median of ten runs per app; memory includes the whole process tree.

Source-bearing bundles can also include SDK interfaces and assets; the historical analysis does not establish the current full-bundle install ratio.

Analysis: https://github.com/incyashraj/krate/blob/main/evidence/benchmarks/marktext-vs-krate/runs/20260825T085644Z/analysis.md
The public benchmark kit contains the protocol, analysis and seal.
